I ran the citations through Redline. All the F.3d cases exist and none is overruled. The Redline database can't confirm what a case holds or whether a pin cite is accurate, so I'm drafting now and using only the cases I'm confident address waiver.

**ARGUMENT**

**I. [Movant] Waived Any Right to Compel Arbitration by Litigating in Federal Court Before Invoking It.**

A right to arbitrate, like any contractual right, can be waived. This Court has long held that a party waives its right to a stay or to compel arbitration "by so substantially utilizing the litigation machinery that to subsequently permit arbitration would prejudice the party opposing the stay." *Am. Recovery Corp. v. Computerized Thermal Imaging, Inc.*, 96 F.3d 88, 95 (4th Cir. 1996); *accord MicroStrategy, Inc. v. Lauricia*, 268 F.3d 244, 249–51 (4th Cir. 2001); *Patten Grading & Paving, Inc. v. Skanska USA Bldg., Inc.*, 380 F.3d 200, 204 (4th Cir. 2004). The federal policy favoring arbitration does not displace that rule. It puts arbitration on equal footing with other contracts, and ordinary contracts can be waived. *See Chorley Enters., Inc. v. Dickey's Barbecue Rests., Inc.*, 807 F.3d 553, 563 (4th Cir. 2015).

**A. The governing standard focuses on the movant's conduct.**

The Supreme Court has clarified the waiver inquiry. In *Morgan v. Sundance, Inc.*, 596 U.S. 411, 419 (2022), it held that courts may not condition waiver of an arbitration right on a showing of prejudice. Waiver turns on whether the party knowingly relinquished the right, as shown by acting inconsistently with it. To the extent *American Recovery*, *MicroStrategy*, and *Patten Grading* treat prejudice as a separate element, *Morgan* abrogated that part of them. Their description of what counts as litigation conduct inconsistent with arbitration remains instructive. [Movant] waived its right under either framework.

**B. [Movant] acted inconsistently with the right to arbitrate.**

[Movant] had the arbitration agreement from the outset. Yet it [filed an answer without asserting arbitration / moved to dismiss on the merits / participated in discovery for ___ months / sought a ruling on the merits]. *See Patten Grading*, 380 F.3d at 204–07 (finding waiver where the movant litigated and delayed before invoking arbitration). A party that tests the court's willingness to rule in its favor and demands arbitration only after an adverse result has chosen the forum and cannot undo that choice. [Movant]'s conduct went well beyond the limited early steps this Court has found compatible with preserving arbitration. *Cf. MicroStrategy*, 268 F.3d at 249–51; *Am. Recovery*, 96 F.3d at 95–96.

**C. Even under the pre-*Morgan* framework, permitting arbitration would prejudice [Defendant].**

Under this Court's prior cases, prejudice may arise from delay, from expense incurred in litigating, or from the movant's use of litigation procedures that would be unavailable in arbitration. *See Patten Grading*, 380 F.3d at 205–06. [Defendant] has [incurred $___ in fees defending the merits / responded to ___ discovery requests / briefed dispositive motions]. Forcing [Defendant] to start over before an arbitral panel would waste those resources and reward [Movant] for using the court's processes selectively. [Movant] also obtained [discovery / rulings] it could not have obtained in arbitration.

**D. The district court's waiver finding should be reviewed with deference to its factual findings.**

Whether a party waived arbitration is reviewed de novo as a question of law, but the underlying factual findings about the course of litigation are reviewed for clear error. *See Patten Grading*, 380 F.3d at 204; *MicroStrategy*, 268 F.3d at 249. The record here supports the finding of waiver, and the order denying arbitration should be affirmed.
